# gbulletair89 v1.2

Small C89 fixed-point synthesizer for bullets passing through air: subsonic whiz, transonic zip and supersonic ballistic crack.

Version 1.2 darkens the aerodynamic noise so it no longer reads as exposed white noise. It adds a dedicated two-pole body low-pass, retunes the six-band EQ toward low-mid body, and slightly extends the ADSR attack while preserving the independent supersonic crack.

## Constraints

- C89 / `-std=c89 -pedantic`
- No `malloc`, `realloc`, `free` or heap use
- No `float` or `double`
- Core library includes no `stdio.h`, `stdlib.h` or `math.h`
- Static, caller-owned state
- 48 kHz, 16-bit output
- CC0-1.0

The demo uses `stdio.h` only to write WAV files. It is not part of the runtime core.

## v1.2 signal path

```text
white noise -> swept HP/LP body -> ADSR + flutter
           -> two-pole body low-pass -> ballistic crack
           -> six-band EQ -> drive/soft clip -> subtle chorus
           -> stereo multi-tap reverb -> trajectory pan
```

The new body low-pass is applied only to the aerodynamic noise layer. The ballistic N-wave crack is added afterward, so filtering the white-noise hiss does not erase the supersonic transient.

The six equalizer gains are Q12 values. `4096` is unity gain. Version 1.2 raises low/mid bands and attenuates air/ultra bands more strongly than v1.1.

## Presets

| Index | Preset | Character |
|---:|---|---|
| 0 | `SUBSONIC_WHIZ` | Rounded aerodynamic pass with a soft top end |
| 1 | `TRANSONIC_ZIP` | Compact mid-focused zip with weak transient |
| 2 | `SUPERSONIC_SNAP` | Clear crack over a controlled air body |
| 3 | `CLOSE_RIFLE_PASS` | Strong near-miss snap and dense midrange tear |
| 4 | `HEAVY_ROUND_PASS` | Darkest, heaviest body and long tail |
| 5 | `DISTANT_CRACK` | Thin crack with restrained high-frequency hiss |
| 6 | `INDOOR_PASS` | Warm room reflections and reduced white-noise edge |
| 7 | `GAME_WHIZZ` | Most present preset, still filtered for gameplay clarity |

## Minimal integration

```c
#include "gbulletair89.h"

static gba89_state bullet_voice;
static gba89_s16 stereo_buffer[512 * 2];

void audio_init(void)
{
    gba89_init(&bullet_voice, 0x1234UL);
}

void play_near_miss(void)
{
    gba89_trigger_preset(&bullet_voice, GBA89_PRESET_CLOSE_RIFLE_PASS);
}

void audio_callback(void)
{
    gba89_render_stereo(&bullet_voice, stereo_buffer, 512UL);
}
```

## Custom sound

Copy a preset returned by `gba89_get_preset()`, edit its integer fields and call `gba89_trigger()`.

Important controls:

- `attack_ms`, `decay_ms`, `sustain_ms`, `release_ms`: aerodynamic body envelope.
- `hp_*_q15`, `lp_*_q15`: first swept band-shaping stage.
- `body_lp_q15`: two-pole body filter coefficient. Lower values are darker; larger values open the high end.
- `eq_sub_q12` through `eq_ultra_q12`: six fixed EQ bands; `4096` is unity.
- `reverb_mix_q15`, `reverb_feedback_q15`, `reverb_tail_ms`: reflected field and post-envelope decay.
- `crack_level_q15`, `crack_delay_ms`, `crack_samples`: ballistic N-wave.
- `drive_q8_8`: `256` = 1.0x drive, `512` = 2.0x.
- `pan_start_q15`, `pan_end_q15`: trajectory from left to right or vice versa.

## Build

```sh
make
make preview
./test_c89
```

MinGW32:

```bat
build_mingw32.bat
```

## Runtime memory

One voice owns:

- 256-sample chorus buffer: 512 bytes
- 2048-sample reflection buffer: 4096 bytes
- Five fixed-point EQ memories
- Two fixed-point body-filter memories
- State, filters and configuration: implementation-dependent small overhead

No hidden allocation occurs.

## Validation performed for this package

- Core and test compiled with `-std=c89 -pedantic -Wall -Wextra -Werror -O2`.
- Forbidden-token scan found no dynamic allocation calls or floating-point types in `include/`, `src/` or `tests/`.
- Eight individual stereo WAV previews and one combined showcase were generated by the C demo.
- Preview scan found no clipped PCM samples.
